evals.prompt: Create an Archloom architecture diagram and request flow for a fictional web app: Browser sends GET /records to API, API reads Database, Database returns rows, API returns JSON. Group Client, Application and Storage. Add summaries and step notes. Produce validated JSON, SVGs, atlas and an offline HTML canvas. No icons or external services are needed.
evals.expected_output: Three real components, browser-to-API HTTP edge, API-to-database read-only data edge, ordered four-message request/return flow and locally rendered artifacts.
expectations: Graph validates against the public architecture-only contract.
Includes exactly the requested components and their three correct lane groups.
Directed relationships match the described HTTP/read or asynchronous job/write operations.
Flow participants and ordered messages match the described journey with correct response/async kinds.
Lanes, nodes and flows have summaries; every message has a step note.
Every expected SVG and atlas is present and equals a fresh authoritative render.
Offline HTML is complete, deterministic and uses a network-denying CSP.

evals.prompt: Create an Archloom diagram for a fictional scheduled job system: Scheduler publishes a task to Queue, Queue delivers the task asynchronously to Worker, Worker saves the result in Object Store. Group Control, Processing and Storage. Include a representative ordered flow with notes and summaries. Produce validated JSON, SVGs, atlas and an offline HTML canvas; do not label the result write read-only. No icons or external services are needed.
evals.expected_output: Four components, queue/event delivery with async messages, a writable data edge to storage, a flow following the declared ordering and locally rendered artifacts.
expectations: Graph validates against the public architecture-only contract.
